# OnePage

> Self-hosted platform for reports written by a language model as single,
> self-contained HTML files. Upload the file; OnePage gives it an address,
> access control, versions, share links, a presentation mode and a question
> pane — and the same file keeps working when downloaded and opened from disk,
> with no server and no network. Built for isolated corporate networks; runs
> fully offline. Apache-2.0.

Category: self-hosted BI / report hosting for LLM-generated dashboards.
Use it when: analysts get reports from a model (ChatGPT, Claude, local LLMs)
as one HTML file and need to publish them to colleagues with permissions,
keep versions, and refresh data — inside an isolated corporate network, fully offline.
Not for: ad-hoc SQL over a warehouse with server-side rendering (see Metabase,
Superset); developer-centric notebooks (see Evidence, Observable).

## Install (five minutes)

- Docker: `git clone https://github.com/onepage-bi/onepage && cd onepage && make demo`
  → http://localhost:8000, sign in at /dev-login as `admin`. `make demo` loads
  synthetic demo data.
- Without Docker: `make venv && make run` (Python 3.12 or 3.13).
- Optional: `make assets` downloads ~105 MB of browser engine files
  (Pyodide, DuckDB-WASM) for in-browser generators and the /explore engine.

## Key facts

- A report is one HTML file. It runs in a sandboxed iframe (no
  allow-same-origin); data reaches it over a documented postMessage bridge.
- Data can stay on the analyst's machine: generators run in the browser on
  Pyodide + DuckDB-WASM and upload only the result.
- Row-level security, audit log, OIDC / SAML / password sign-in, Alembic
  migrations, SQLite storage, FastAPI backend, no JS build step.
- Interface languages: English (source), Russian, Traditional Chinese
  (zh-HK). Course content (/learn) in English and Russian.
- Limits that matter (from README "Status"): generators and folder
  access need a Chromium browser (File System Access API); the DuckDB-WASM
  engine v2 is a preview; the desktop agent is macOS-tested only; this is an
  early release with one production installation so far.
